sections.overview: This phytophagous ladybird is associated with bryony and is recorded across parts of Europe. GBIF lists English, French, German and Spanish common names.
sections.identification: It is orange to brick red with eleven black elytral spots. The British account gives a length of 5–7 mm.
sections.habitat: In Picardy it occurs in moist valleys and coastal dunes where white bryony grows.
sections.diet: Picardy adults and larvae feed exclusively on white bryony. British sources report melon feeding elsewhere in Europe.
sections.behavior: In Picardy, records peak from May to August.
sections.reproduction: The species is phytophagous throughout its larval and adult stages; British records document it breeding at Molesey.
sections.ecology: The French profile distinguishes it from H. angusticollis and H. elaterii; the latter has larger spots.
sections.conservation: It is unevaluated nationally in France; Picardy reports local Least Concern.
